_meta.purpose: HELD-OUT evaluation set. Exists so that improvements made while looking at gold_set.json can be reported with an honest generalization number instead of a score on the set they were tuned against.
_meta.discipline: Written AFTER fixes 1-3 were designed, from documents that contribute to NO question in gold_set.json. Nothing in these documents was inspected while diagnosing the INT4 failures.
_meta.why_prose_only:
NUMERIC HELD-OUT QUESTIONS ARE NOT INCLUDED, AND THAT IS ITSELF A FINDING. Table extraction on these documents is too corrupted to serve as ground truth: sampled cells carry row labels like 'Billion $53', '9 Billion', '0 Billion', '2023 and 2024', and values like '024.' and '2024.'. They are text-fallback tables whose labels fragmented (defect class L2/L3 in results/known_limitations.md). Writing numeric questions against them would measure extraction quality, not model quality, and any score would be uninterpretable.

The corollary is a sampling bias in the ORIGINAL gold set that should be stated plainly in the memo: all 8 of its numeric questions come from the FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, because FDIC is the only corpus document whose multi-section tables survived extraction cleanly enough to key questions against. So gold-set numeric accuracy describes performance on well-extracted tables, not on this corpus as a whole.

questions.note: Deliberately pairs two unrelated sectors. A multi-doc path that only retrieves topically-similar documents will fail this, which is the point: it tests whether the path can genuinely combine two sources rather than finding one document that looks like it covers both.
